svg.aria-label: STM32MP157F-DK2 boot chain: the Boot ROM loads TF-A BL2 from the fsbl1 partition into on-chip SYSRAM; BL2 sets up the DDR3 memory and loads OP-TEE and U-Boot from the FIP; OP-TEE is both the secure monitor and the SCMI server for clocks, resets and regulators and stays resident; U-Boot runs in the non-secure world, reads extlinux.conf and starts the 32-bit Linux kernel. There is no BL31 on this chip.
svg.text: How the STM32MP157F-DK2 boots, and what this repository builds for each stage
Power-on to login prompt: each stage loads the next. There is no BL31 on this 32-bit chip: OP-TEE is the secure monitor and stays resident.
SECURE WORLD · secure SVC / monitor mode
and for the SD card supply
copies BL2 from partition fsbl1 into SYSRAM and jumps to it (BL2 is built with RESET_TO_BL2: it runs straight after the ROM).
BL2 opens the FIP (found by partition TYPE GUID 19d5df83-…, or the name 'fip') and loads OP-TEE (3 files) and U-Boot + its DTB.
BL2 jumps to OP-TEE; OP-TEE initialises (and starts serving SCMI), then returns to the normal world at U-Boot's entry point.
STILL IN MEMORY WHILE LINUX RUNS
Boot ROM, BL2: finished (SYSRAM is reused)
OP-TEE stays in the secure world for good: it is the monitor, so every SMC goes through it; it serves PSCI and SCMI
No BL31 and no DDR firmware on this chip: the DDR3 driver is part of BL2
Addresses: BL2 from plat/st/stm32mp1/stm32mp1_fip_def.h and the linker map of this build; OP-TEE from fdts/stm32mp15-fw-config.dtsi and plat-stm32mp1/conf.mk;
STM32MP_BL33_BASE (stm32mp1_def.h) and u-boot include/configs/stm32mp15_common.h (kernel_addr_r). Red = secure world, blue = boot stages, teal = Linux, slate = hardware.
